Question kind: M7_Invariants

Question:
Use the FULL test suite in `test/qa/parse_m3u8_attributes_loop_value_invariant_suite_test.py` (all 18 test methods in class `TestParseM3u8AttributesLoopValueInvariantSuiteQA`). Each test method calls `yt_dlp.utils._utils.parse_m3u8_attributes(<attrib>)` (defined at line 4488 in `yt_dlp/utils/_utils.py`) with a different attribute-string literal. The function body is:
```
def parse_m3u8_attributes(attrib):
    info = {}
    for (key, val) in re.findall(r'(?P<key>[A-Z0-9-]+)=(?P<val>"[^"]+"|[^",]+)(?:,|$)', attrib):
        if val.startswith('"'):
            val = val[1:-1]
        info[key] = val
    return info
```
Consider the LOOP INVARIANT to be checked at the END of every iteration body of the for-loop -- specifically, at the line-4493 trace event (`info[key] = val`, the last statement of the body), which fires once per iteration. The candidate invariant is:
    INV(val) := ',' not in val
i.e., the local string variable `val` (after the optional `val = val[1:-1]` strip on line 4492) does NOT contain a comma character. Report whether this invariant is held in EVERY iteration across ALL 18 test calls. Note: an iteration counts even if the test only triggers a single iteration; total iterations observed = sum of for-loop iterations across all tests. Return a JSON object with EXACTLY these three keys:
- `total_iterations_observed`: int -- total number of for-loop iterations completed across all 18 test calls (i.e., total line-4493 trace events).
- `violating_iteration_count`: int -- number of iterations in which INV(val) is FALSE (i.e., `,' in val`).
- `is_invariant_always_held`: bool -- True iff `violating_iteration_count == 0`.

Template answer (must match exactly):
{"is_invariant_always_held":"bool","total_iterations_observed":"int","violating_iteration_count":"int"}

I have the test inputs and the parser logic needed to compute the per-match iterations and comma violations. DONE_WITH_FILE_READING
The loop iterates once for each `(key, val)` pair returned by `re.findall(...)`. For unquoted values, the pattern `[^",]+` excludes commas, so those iterations satisfy the invariant. For quoted values, the pattern can capture commas inside the quotes, and then `val = val[1:-1]` removes only the surrounding quotes, not internal commas. Among the 18 test inputs, the total regex matches sum to 30 iterations, and exactly three quoted values contain commas after stripping: the `CODECS` value in test `c`, the `CODECS` value in test `m`, and the `CODECS` value in test `q`. Therefore the invariant is not always true.
